data.body_html:
Marbella in March 2027: the winter crowds have gone, the almond trees are blooming, and the sun is warm enough to sit on deck without a coat. But is it warm enough for a Marbella boat rental? The short answer: yes, if you pick the right boat and dress in layers. This guide gives you the real numbers – air temperature, sea temperature, wind, and sunshine – so you can decide whether March is your month.

Marbella March Weather: The Numbers

Average daily high in March: 19°C–20°C (66°F–68°F). Overnight lows: 10°C–12°C. Sea temperature: 15°C–16°C. Sunshine: 7–8 hours per day. Rain: 5–6 days in the month, totalling 40–50mm. Wind: typically 10–15 km/h from the west, with occasional Levante (easterly) gusts up to 30 km/h. UV index: 3–4 – bring sunscreen, but you won’t burn quickly.

Sea Temperature in March: Can You Swim?

The Mediterranean off Marbella in March sits at 15°C–16°C. That’s wetsuit territory. Most people can manage a quick dip, but don’t expect a leisurely swim. If your group wants to spend hours in the water, June to September is better. For a March trip, focus on cruising, sunbathing on deck, and enjoying the coastline – the water is for the brave.

Best Boats for March Weather

Choose a boat with a covered cockpit or flybridge for wind protection. Our Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax, €749/2h) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax, €749/2h) both have full enclosures – perfect for early-season comfort. For larger groups, the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) offers both indoor saloon and open flybridge. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax, €4,719/4h including jet ski) has a spacious main deck with wind protection.

Where to Cruise in March

Stick to coastal routes. Head east from Puerto Banús towards Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés – these coves are sheltered from westerly winds. The Marbella Marina front offers views of the Golden Mile and La Concha mountain. For a longer trip, cruise west to Estepona (8 NM) or Sotogrande (18 NM) – both have calm marinas for a stop. Avoid open-water crossings to Africa in March – the Alborán Sea can be choppy.

What to Wear on a March Boat Trip

Layers are non-negotiable. Start with a base layer (long-sleeve merino or synthetic), add a fleece or light jumper, and top with a windproof jacket. Long trousers and closed-toe shoes. Bring a hat and sunglasses – the sun is low but bright. By midday, you can shed layers; by 4pm, put them back on. Our boats provide blankets, but bring your own if you feel the cold.

March vs. April: Which Is Better?

April averages 2°C warmer (16°C–22°C) and sea temps rise to 17°C. Rain drops to 4 days per month. March has fewer crowds and lower prices – Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) are €749/2h year-round, but availability is better in March. If you want warmer swimming, wait until May (sea 19°C). For a quiet, affordable cruise with decent sun, March wins.
